copy_if()
Previously, we learned about the copy() function which copied a range of values to some destination.
But what if we wanted to copy only those elements of the container which satisfies certain conditions.
Let's say we have a vector of integers,
What if we want to copy only the even numbers from the above vector into some other vector. This is where copy_if() comes into play.
The copy_if() function takes an additional parameter, a predicate - a lambda is a good example of a predicate. Let's see the function signature.
copy_if(iterator first, iterator last, new_iterator d_first, predicate pred);
Take it this way, the copy will take place only for those elements where the predicate returns true.
For the above problem of copying only even numbers we only have to write a lambda expression that returns true when its input parameter is even.
Let's now create a new vector of size 5.
vector<int>(5) even_numbers;
To perform the copy operation,
copy_if (numbers.begin(), numbers.end(), even_numbers.begin(), find_even);
What happens here is, every element in the numbers vector is passed one by one to the lambda and only those elements are copied for which the lambda returns true.
